title: Abnormality & Infection
description: Every science has its anomalies: effects that the laws we know cannot explain, systems that copy themselves and refuse to die. Containment failures leave them lying around. Study them properly; how they arise, spread, interact with the normal world, and how they can finally be explained. Unlocks the Anomaly Containment Ward and Contained Anomaly Specimens.

puzzle.goal: Before calling anything abnormal you must know what normal looks like. A quantity measured many times scatters around its mean μ with spread σ, its values distributed as the bell-shaped density exp(−(x − μ)²/2σ²)/(σ√(2π)). Write the probability that a single measurement lies more than k standard deviations from the mean, on either side.
puzzle.name: two-sided tail of the Gaussian distribution (the significance of a deviation)
puzzle.ask: For large k the integral is close to √(2/π)·e^{−k²/2}/k. Physics calls a result a discovery at k = @{k}: find the chance of a deviation that large by accident, in units of 10⁻⁷.

vars.P: probability of a deviation of k σ or more

puzzle.method: The two tails are equal by symmetry: integrate one from μ + kσ to infinity and double it. Substitute u = (x − μ)/σ; for large u the tail integral of e^{−u²/2} is e^{−k²/2}/k.
